plan.title: empty-desert

scenes.heading: 1. EXT. DESERT - DAY
scenes.summary: Wind moves sand across empty desert ground. Sourced action contains no people, vehicles, or stunt activity. Special equipment (e.g. wind machine) is an inferred production possibility.

scenes.heading: 2. EXT. RIDGE - DAY
scenes.summary: Wind moves sand across empty ridge ground. Sourced action contains no people, vehicles, or stunt activity. Special equipment (e.g. wind machine) is an inferred production possibility.

days.label: Day 1 - Desert and Ridge Exterior Landscape Filming
setupRequirements: Camera and grip setup for exterior desert natural landscape capture.
Company move and repositioning between Desert and Ridge exterior setups.
Dust and environmental protection for camera lenses and monitoring gear.
complianceNotes: Filming on public, state, or federal land in New Mexico requires relevant local or BLM/state agency permits prior to production.
Ensure standard general liability insurance coverage is active in accordance with New Mexico local filming jurisdiction requirements.

costDrivers.label: Jurisdictional Filming Permits and Land-Use Fees
costDrivers.reason: Filming exterior scenes in New Mexico across public, municipal, state, or federal BLM land incurs permit application and per-day filming fees depending on specific location jurisdiction.

costDrivers.label: General Liability Insurance Policy
costDrivers.reason: New Mexico jurisdictions typically require proof of comprehensive general liability insurance coverage before issuing filming permits for exterior setups.

costDrivers.label: Local Crew Labor and Payroll Fringes
costDrivers.reason: Crew compensation for a single 8 to 10 hour exterior day includes standard labor rates along with New Mexico payroll burden and workers' compensation requirements.

costDrivers.label: New Mexico Production Tax Credit Applicability
costDrivers.reason: New Mexico offers a refundable tax credit baseline of 25% on qualified spend, though small short-form budgets may face cost-benefit thresholds regarding third-party audit and application requirements.

assumptions: The production consists of a 1-day shoot covering two exterior desert/ridge landscape setups with no cast, stunts, or minor compliance requirements.
A lean camera and grip crew (approximately 3 to 6 technicians) operates within an 8 to 10 hour day.
Locations are accessible via standard vehicle transport without requiring complex heavy-rig logistics or overnight remote basecamps.
Atmospheric effects or wind machines remain an optional production possibility rather than a confirmed requirement.
Insurance costs assume standard short-term commercial production general liability coverage compliant with New Mexico jurisdictional minimums.

locations.name: Bureau of Land Management Public Lands (Rio Puerco / Albuquerque Area)
locations.fit: Matches both Scene 1 (EXT. DESERT) and Scene 2 (EXT. RIDGE) requiring open desert terrain, ridges, and windblown landscape without constructed sets or modern fixtures.
risks: Permits are not confirmed and require advance coordination with the BLM Rio Puerco Field Office for minimum-impact or commercial filming authorization.
Federal land use authorization lead times can vary and strict environmental or minimum impact determinations apply.
Exposed outdoor desert and ridge environments introduce risks of dust intrusion on camera gear and unpredictable wind/weather conditions.

locations.name: Santa Fe County Open Space and Desert Ridge Terrain
locations.fit: Provides natural desert and ridge landscape visual aesthetics suited for capturing daytime exterior landscape plates and sand movement in close proximity to production infrastructure.
risks: Permits are required for both public and private land filming via the Santa Fe Film Office and are unconfirmed.
Production must meet standard New Mexico general liability insurance thresholds ($1,050,000 standard) and local application fees.
Outdoor ridge terrain may involve elevation, access challenges for support gear, and exposure to wind gusts.

locations.name: Doña Ana County Desert and BLM Public Lands (Las Cruces District)
locations.fit: Offers extensive arid desert ground and natural ridge formations suitable for Scene 1 and Scene 2 landscape cinematography.
risks: Filming permits must be cleared through Film Las Cruces, Doña Ana County, or the BLM Las Cruces Field Office; authorization is not pre-approved.
Advance notification requirements may apply depending on staging proximity to adjacent properties or roadways.
Remote desert terrain increases logistical transit time and presents environmental exposure risks.

research.title: New Mexico Film Incentives | Tax Credits & Rebates | Cast & Crew
research.excerpt: A declaration of residency form is required to be completed by all residents except extras. ## \+ QUALIFIED SPEND Qualified spend includes “direct production expenditures” that are subject to taxation in NM along with all wages paid to NM residents, nonresident performing artists, and a limited amount/number of nonresident below-the-line (BTL). The amount of nonresident BTL wages that may qualify is capped at 15% of the total budgeted amount of NM BTL crew wages (for film partners the NRCE credit is still 15%, but nonresident wages claimed cannot exceed resident wages claimed). The size of the budget determines the number of nonresident BTL that may be included in the calculation. Payments made to ANY nonresident performing artist are subject to 5.9% withholding. Nonresident performing artists hired via their loan out company must go thru a “super loan out” company (ask about using Cast & Crew’s SLO). ... (2) The credit that may be earned on payments to nonresident principal performing artists is capped at $5 million in the aggregate (an additional $10 million is available for film partner productions. The $10 million per production caps are then capped in aggregate at $40 million per fiscal year). (3) Third-party audit is required when the claim exceeds $5 million. research.title: Permit Information | New Mexico Film Office
research.excerpt: # Permit Information Although comparatively few permits are necessary for filming in New Mexico, permits are required for production on federal, state-owned, and tribal properties and lands. Permits are also often required for production on city properties, especially historical sites, and public streets, as well as for special use of county roads and state highways. **\*** Companies considering shooting on federal property must connect with the proper federal contact. * * * ### Location Permits * The New Mexico Film Office does not issue filming permits. * Film permitting is generally handled by the city/town/county where you're filming. For permit questions specific to a location, please get in touch with the nearest film liaison. * State-owned properties: Please contact the NMFO at 505-476-5600 or via email at info@nmfilm.com * * * ### Railroad Right of Entry and Permitting Please get in touch with the [NMDOT Rail Bureau | NMDOT](https://www.dot.nm. gov/planning-research-multimodal-and-safety/modal/transit-rail/rail-bureau/) via email with any inquiries or questions about potential encroachment on railroad property. If you are within 100 feet of a railroad or between a fence/property marker and a railroad, you may be trespassing in the railroad right-of-way and can conflict with railroad operations which can create a serious safety hazard for the railroad and film production. This includes production at NM Rail Runner Express stations and Amtrak Stations. Filming activities may be interrupted if you fail to obtain written permission from the railroad owner to enter its property. In New Mexico, the three most prominent railroad property owners are BNSF Railway, Union Pacific Railroad, and the New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT). research.title: Permits - Film Las Cruces
research.excerpt: Film Las Cruces is contracted with the City of Las Cruces, Doña Ana County and the City of Anthony to provide permitting assistance to film and digital media projects. We are happy to walk you through and point you in the right direction for all other permitting agencies throughout southern New Mexico; including White Sands National Park, Town of Mesilla, Bureau of Land Management, Spaceport America, Hatch, New Mexico Department of Transportation, and others. ##### What kinds of filming activities do not require a permit? News and gathering of news related stories. Other types of documentaries not requiring the use of actors, models, sets, or props. Still not sure if your production requires a filming permit? Give us a call: 575-805-3456 ##### What is a low impact/b-roll permit? A low impact/b-roll filming permit may be issued for documentary-style footage with a maximum of 8 total cast and crew on-site at any one time. ##### When should I notify neighboring residents and businesses regarding filming activity in the area? All permitted filming locations are likely to require the surrounding businesses and neighbors to be notified of your filming activity 48 hours in advance of load in. The standard radius for notification letter distribution is 200 feet from the filming location, parking, and basecamp. Film Las Cruces will notify your production with notification requirements during the process of your application. ## Submit a Permit Application [Privacy Policy](https://filmlascruces.com/privacy-policy/) | [Terms & Conditions](https://filmlascruces.com/terms-and-conditions/) Film Las Cruces Manage Cookie Consent To provide the best experiences, we use technologies like cookies to store and/or access device information.
